# Omnichannel Engagement Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Omnichannel Engagement Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness. Building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved engagement environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded analytics files, the proposed aggregate feeds and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger. Record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the aggregate CRM and commerce analytics and the contact-center analytics feed. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare experience, digital, contact-center and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview, not publication. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files, with no PAC CLI or YAML import. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Consent and frequency ownership | Have engagement owners define consent, optional-preference and frequency-cap rules before any experiment uses customer data. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer experience business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Broken handoffs, repeated context and inconsistent engagement across channels. Agree the starting friction before judging channel experiments or engagement changes.

Fill your baseline record:

| Journey or channel | Measurement period | Handoff breaks | Repeated-context contacts | Consent coverage | Data source | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree engagement replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer experience business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Customer experience business owner | Approve analytics sources, engagement scope and the review workflow; agree production success measures without treating synthetic metrics as results. |
| Authorized engagement reviewers | Review aggregate insights and approve any experiment with consent, optional preferences and frequency caps preserved. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing and capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any analytics connection is approved. |
| Analytics connection owners | Approve the read-only aggregate CRM, commerce and contact-center feeds; record connection identities and least-privilege references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check OCE-01 through OCE-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; fail any person-level output or claimed outreach. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route engagement decisions to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Engagement replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The experience owner records where handoffs break and context is repeated today before choosing measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/omnichannel-engagement/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access to aggregate analytics only.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/omnichannel-engagement/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/omnichannel-engagement/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/omnichannel-engagement/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/omnichannel-engagement/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Omnichannel Engagement Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_omnichannel-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_omnichannel-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: campaign-attribution
9. Add skill: channel-performance
10. Add skill: engagement-optimization
11. Add skill: journey-analysis
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass OCE-01: Customer Experience Leader
15. Pass OCE-02: Contact Center Supervisor
16. Pass OCE-03: Digital Engagement Manager
17. Pass OCE-04: Digital Engagement Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: OCE-01, OCE-02, OCE-03, OCE-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `OmnichannelEngagementAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The optional Brainstem lane is recorded as used or skipped; no workshop step depends on it.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged engagement prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full response; annotated screenshots do not replace the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before showing channel, campaign or journey analytics. Request only read scopes for approved aggregate feeds; exclude person-level data. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved aggregate CRM and commerce analytics

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Analytics connection owners

1. **Bind Approved aggregate CRM and commerce analytics — read:** Bind scoped read-only aggregate connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Approved aggregate CRM and commerce analytics:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved aggregate CRM and commerce analytics:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved aggregate CRM and commerce analytics:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Claim no live KPIs; the figures are fixed synthetic aggregates. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Stop and request a valid identifier; never approximate.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved contact-center analytics

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Analytics connection owners

1. **Bind Approved contact-center analytics — read:** Add a governed aggregate feed as approved knowledge or read-only actions.

2. **Identity for Approved contact-center analytics:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved contact-center analytics:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved contact-center analytics:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Stitch no identities; return aggregate channel evidence only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Decline and return aggregate evidence; never stitch identities or infer traits.

### Step 3-3. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Analytics connection owners

Bind only approved read-only aggregate feeds with dedicated references; keep all write actions separate.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Only approved read-only connections are bound, and all write actions stay separate.
- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no live metric or outreach is claimed without tool evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Before rollout, test an approved test deployment as experience, digital and contact-center users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data measures; fictional ROAS, ROI and conversion figures are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked engagement corpus | All four cases, OCE-01 through OCE-04, include every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Privacy and no-outreach boundary | Any identity stitching, sensitive inference, outreach, offer, reward, record change or purchase is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a positive target-state anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required images. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer experience business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Customer experience business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved engagement audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed engagement sessions, their transcripts, tool connection and authentication errors, and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
